chunks: "I'd treat rework as a user of the board.

First, space : leave a keepout around large or hidden-joint parts like BGAs and QFNs so a nozzle can sit over them without heating or blowing away neighbours, and keep tall parts like electrolytic caps or connectors away.
Second, heat : use thermal reliefs on pads tied to big planes so the joint can reach solder temperature, but not on high-current or exposed thermal pads, where I'd rely on preheat.
Third, put the likely changes into the design : a footprint for an alternate pull-up, zero-ohm links to isolate a rail, and test points near the nets I'd probe.

Fourth, don't hide anything : no parts or test points under a BGA on the other side where I'd need to reach them, and keep heavy parts off the bottom below a rework area, because they can fall off when the board is reheated.
Fifth, clear markings : silkscreen pin 1 and polarity outside the part body and reference designators that aren't covered.
And for the big parts, I'd avoid via-in-pad or use filled and capped vias so solder doesn't wick away, and I'd keep the footprint to IPC land-pattern recommendations so the rework joint is standard."
